question: Which among the following is a river that originates in the Western Ghats?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mandovi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mandovi River (also known as the Mahadayi) originates in the Western Ghats, near Bhimgad in the Belagavi district of Karnataka, and flows through Goa before draining into the Arabian Sea at Mormugao harbour. (मांडवी नदी — पश्चिमी घाट)

 

• It is one of the two principal rivers of Goa, along with the Zuari, and together they enclose several islands, including Divar and Chorao.

 

• Narmada, by contrast, originates from the Amarkantak Plateau in Madhya Pradesh, not the Western Ghats.

 

• Luni and Banas both originate in the Aravalli Range of Rajasthan — Luni near Pushkar (Ajmer) and Banas near the Khamnor Hills (Rajsamand).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Western Ghats (Sahyadri) run parallel to India's west coast through Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala, and are recognised as a UNESCO World Heritage Site and global biodiversity hotspot.

 

• Other major rivers originating in the Western Ghats include the Godavari, Krishna, Kaveri, Tungabhadra and Periyar.

 

NOTE

 

• Narmada (Option 1): Originates at Amarkantak in the Maikala Range, Madhya Pradesh, and flows westward into the Gulf of Khambhat, Arabian Sea.

 

• Luni (Option 2): Originates near Pushkar in the Aravalli Range, Rajasthan; a seasonal, saline river that drains into the Rann of Kutch.

 

• Banas (Option 3): Originates in the Khamnor Hills of the Aravalli Range, Rajasthan, and is a tributary of the Chambal River.

question: Among the following, in which material the speed of sound is highest? (at 25°C)
solution_text:
The correct answer is Aluminium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Speed of sound in a solid depends on its stiffness (elastic modulus) and density, approximately given by v = √(E/ρ) — a stiffer, lighter material transmits sound faster. (ध्वनि की चाल)

 

• Among common metals, Aluminium has one of the highest speeds of sound, about 6,420 m/s at 25°C, due to its favourable stiffness-to-density ratio.

 

• Steel (~5,960 m/s) and Iron (~5,120 m/s) transmit sound more slowly than Aluminium, and Nickel also falls below Aluminium's typical reference value.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• Speed of sound is generally highest in solids, lower in liquids, and lowest in gases, because of the differing strength of intermolecular bonding.

 

• The speed of sound in air at 25°C is about 346 m/s — far lower than in any of the metals listed here.

 

NOTE

 

• Nickel (Option 1): Speed of sound is around 4,900–6,000 m/s depending on form — lower than Aluminium's standard reference value.

 

• Steel (Option 2): Speed of sound is about 5,960 m/s, lower than Aluminium.

 

• Iron (Option 3): Speed of sound is about 5,120 m/s, the lowest among the four options given.

question: The second five-year plan of India focused on ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is rapid industrialization.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Second Five-Year Plan (1956–61) was based on the Mahalanobis model (devised by economist P.C. Mahalanobis), which prioritised rapid industrialization, with special emphasis on developing heavy and basic industries. (द्वितीय पंचवर्षीय योजना — तीव्र औद्योगीकरण)

 

• Major public-sector steel plants — at Bhilai, Durgapur and Rourkela — were set up during this period as part of this industrial push.

 

• It marked a deliberate shift from the First Plan's agriculture-and-irrigation focus toward building India's capital goods and industrial base.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The First Five-Year Plan (1951–56) focused on agriculture and irrigation and was based on the Harrod–Domar growth model.

 

• The Planning Commission was replaced by NITI Aayog in January 2015, ending the Five-Year Plan era after the Twelfth Plan (2012–17).

 

NOTE

 

• Foreign direct investment (Option 2): Not the stated objective of the Second Plan; FDI liberalisation became prominent only after the 1991 economic reforms.

 

• Balance of payment (Option 3): The Second Plan actually triggered a balance-of-payments crisis due to import-heavy industrialization — this was a challenge it faced, not its guiding focus.

 

• Family Planning Programmes (Option 4): India's Family Planning Programme was launched in 1952, during the First Plan, not as the Second Plan's defining focus.

question: ______ came into existence on 12 July 1982 by transferring the agricultural credit functions of RBI and refinance functions of the then Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation.
option_1: Securities and Exchange Board of India
option_2: Small Industries Development Bank of India
option_4: National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• NABARD was established on 12 July 1982 under the NABARD Act, 1981, by transferring the agricultural credit functions of RBI and the refinance functions of the erstwhile Agricultural Refinance and Development Corporation (ARDC). (राष्ट्रीय कृषि और ग्रामीण विकास बैंक)

 

• It is the apex development bank in India for agriculture and rural development, headquartered in Mumbai.

 

• NABARD supervises Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), State Cooperative Banks and District Central Cooperative Banks, and administers the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• NABARD was set up on the recommendation of the Shivaraman Committee.

 

• It plays a central role in refinancing rural credit institutions and promoting rural development schemes, including watershed development and self-help groups.

 

NOTE

 

• Securities and Exchange Board of India (Option 1): The regulator of India's securities markets, established in 1988 and given statutory powers in 1992; unrelated to agricultural credit.

 

• Small Industries Development Bank of India (Option 2): The apex institution for financing and promoting Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs), established in 1990.

 

• Reserve Bank of India (Option 3): India's central bank, established in 1935; it transferred its direct agricultural credit functions to NABARD in 1982 rather than retaining them.

question: Which of the following was the runners-up at Durand Cup 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mumbai City FC.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 Durand Cup final was contested between Bengaluru FC and Mumbai City FC.

 

• Bengaluru FC won 2–1, with goals from Sivasakthi Narayanan and Alan Costa, claiming their first-ever Durand Cup title, while Mumbai City FC scored through Apuia. (डूरंड कप 2022 — उपविजेता)

 

• Mumbai City FC finished as the runner-up of the tournament.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Durand Cup is Asia's oldest football tournament and the world's third-oldest, first held in 1888; it is named after Sir Mortimer Durand.

 

• The 2022 edition was co-hosted across Kolkata, Guwahati and Imphal.

 

NOTE

 

• Kerala Blasters (Option 1): A Kochi-based ISL club that did not reach the 2022 Durand Cup final.

 

• Bengaluru FC (Option 3): Actually the winner of the 2022 Durand Cup, having defeated Mumbai City FC in the final — not the runner-up.

 

• Mohammedan SC (Option 4): A historic Kolkata-based club that took part in the tournament but was not a 2022 finalist.

question: Kalsubai peak is located in which of the following Indian states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kalsubai Peak, located in the Western Ghats in Ahmednagar district, Maharashtra, is the highest peak in Maharashtra at 1,646 metres. (कळसुबाई शिखर — महाराष्ट्र)

 

• It lies within the Kalsubai Harishchandragad Wildlife Sanctuary and is often called the “Everest of Maharashtra.”

 

• A temple dedicated to the goddess Kalsubai stands at its summit, and the peak is a popular trekking destination.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Maharashtra's other notable peaks include Salher (the second-highest) and Mahabaleshwar.

 

• The Western Ghats, which run through Maharashtra, are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a major biodiversity hotspot.

 

NOTE

 

• Madhya Pradesh (Option 1): Its highest peak is Dhupgarh in the Satpura Range.

 

• Andhra Pradesh (Option 3): Its highest peak is Arma Konda in the Eastern Ghats.

 

• Himachal Pradesh (Option 4): Home to much higher Himalayan peaks, such as Reo Purgyil, part of the Greater Himalayas.

question: As of 2022, there are ______ states in India.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 28.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• As of 2022, India comprises 28 states and 8 Union Territories, a structure in place since 31 October 2019, when Jammu and Kashmir was reorganised into two Union Territories (J&K and Ladakh). (भारत में 28 राज्य)

 

• Before this reorganisation, India had 29 states and 7 Union Territories.

 

• The most recent state to be formed before this change was Telangana, carved out of Andhra Pradesh on 2 June 2014.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The eight Union Territories (as of 2022) are: Andaman & Nicobar Islands, Chandigarh, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Daman & Diu, Delhi (NCT), Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, Lakshadweep, and Puducherry.

 

• Article 1 of the Constitution describes India as a “Union of States.”

 

NOTE

 

• 30 (Option 1): Incorrect figure; India has never had 30 states.

 

• 31 (Option 3): Incorrect; not the current or any recent state count.

 

• 29 (Option 4): Was correct before 31 October 2019, when Jammu and Kashmir still held state status; outdated as of 2022.

question: Which among the following won the best film (critics') award in the 67th Filmfare Awards 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sardar Udham.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• At the 67th Filmfare Awards (2022), Sardar Udham (directed by Shoojit Sircar, starring Vicky Kaushal) won the Critics' Award for Best Film. (सर्वश्रेष्ठ फिल्म — समीक्षक पुरस्कार)

 

• The regular (popular) Best Film award at the same ceremony went to Shershaah.

 

• Sardar Udham, a biographical film on revolutionary Udham Singh, was widely praised for its direction, cinematography and screenplay.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 67th Filmfare Awards ceremony was held in August 2022 in Mumbai.

 

• Ranveer Singh (*83*) and Kriti Sanon (*Mimi*) won the Best Actor and Best Actress (popular) awards that year.

 

NOTE

 

• Sherni (Option 1): A 2021 film starring Vidya Balan; well-received but not the winner of the Critics' Best Film award.

 

• Sandeep Aur Pinky Farar (Option 3): A 2021 film starring Arjun Kapoor and Parineeti Chopra; nominated in various categories but did not win Best Film (Critics).

 

• Ramprasad ki Tehrvi (Option 4): A 2021 Seema Pahwa-directed film, critically appreciated but not this award's winner.

question: Which among the following is India’s first indigenously developed COVID-19 vaccine?
solution_text:
The correct answer is COVAXIN.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• COVAXIN is India's first indigenously developed COVID-19 vaccine, created by Bharat Biotech in collaboration with the Indian Council of Medical Research (ICMR) – National Institute of Virology (NIV), Pune. (कोवैक्सीन — भारत की पहली स्वदेशी कोविड वैक्सीन)

 

• It is a whole-virion inactivated vaccine and received Emergency Use Authorisation in India in January 2021.

 

• It was administered widely as part of India's national COVID-19 vaccination drive, alongside Covishield.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Covishield is the Indian-manufactured (Serum Institute of India) version of the Oxford–AstraZeneca vaccine formula developed in the UK, not an indigenous Indian formulation.

 

• India also developed ZyCoV-D (Zydus Cadila), the world's first DNA-based COVID-19 vaccine, approved later in 2021.

 

NOTE

 

• Sputnik V (Option 1): A Russian-developed vaccine used in India under import/licensing arrangements.

 

• Covishield (Option 2): Manufactured in India but based on the AstraZeneca–Oxford formula developed abroad, so not indigenously developed.

 

• Novavax (Option 4): A US-developed protein subunit vaccine, marketed in India as Covovax.

question: Which of the following is used to view pages and navigate the World Wide Web?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Web Browser.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Web Browser (e.g., Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari) is a software application used to access, retrieve and navigate pages on the World Wide Web. (वेब ब्राउज़र)

 

• It interprets HTML, CSS and JavaScript received from a web server and renders web pages for the user, communicating over the HTTP/HTTPS protocols.

 

• Browsers allow users to follow hyperlinks, use tabs and bookmarks, and move through browsing history to navigate between pages.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The first web browser, WorldWideWeb (later renamed Nexus), was created by Tim Berners-Lee in 1990.

 

• Popular modern browsers include Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge, Safari and Opera.

 

NOTE

 

• Hyperlink (Option 1): A clickable reference embedded in a web page that leads to another page or resource — not the software used for browsing.

 

• World Wide Web (Option 3): The system of interlinked hypertext documents accessed via the Internet — it is what is being browsed, not the tool used to browse it.

 

• Joystick (Option 4): An input/pointing hardware device mainly used for gaming, unrelated to web navigation.

question: Which among the following forts was principal capital of Qutb Shahi dynasty in Hyderabad?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Golconda Fort.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Golconda Fort, near Hyderabad in present-day Telangana, served as the principal capital of the Qutb Shahi dynasty from 1518 until 1590, when the capital was shifted to the newly founded city of Hyderabad. (गोलकोंडा किला — कुतुब शाही वंश की राजधानी)

 

• The Qutb Shahi dynasty was founded by Sultan Quli Qutb-ul-Mulk and was one of the five Deccan Sultanates.

 

• Golconda was also historically renowned as a global trading centre for diamonds, including gems believed to have passed through the region such as the Kohinoor.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Qutb Shahi tombs, standing near Golconda Fort, are associated with the dynasty's rulers.

 

• The Charminar, built by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah in 1591, marks the founding of Hyderabad city.

 

NOTE

 

• Chiktan Fort (Option 1): Located in Ladakh, associated with the Namgyal dynasty of Ladakh — unrelated to the Qutb Shahis.

 

• Rajgad Fort (Option 2): Located in Maharashtra, served as an early capital of the Maratha Empire under Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.

 

• Red Fort (Option 3): Located in Delhi, built by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan as the residence of the Mughal emperors.

question: Which among the following is not a type of Right to freedom in the Indian constitution?
option_1: Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.
option_2: Protection of life and personal liberty.
option_4: Protection in respect of conviction for offences.
solution_text:
The correct answer is offences for armed assembly.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Right to Freedom under the Indian Constitution is covered by Articles 19 to 22: Article 19 (six freedoms, including speech and expression), Article 20 (protection in respect of conviction for offences), Article 21 (protection of life and personal liberty), and Article 22 (protection against arrest and detention in certain cases). (स्वतंत्रता का अधिकार — अनुच्छेद 19–22)

 

• Article 19(1)(b) actually guarantees the right “to assemble peaceably and without arms” — there is no constitutional provision framed as “offences for armed assembly,” so this phrase does not correspond to any genuine Article 19–22 right.

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 correctly describe recognised Rights to Freedom (the marginal headings of Articles 19, 21 and 20 respectively), while Option 3 is not an actual constitutional right.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 21A (Right to Education), inserted by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002, is also closely linked with this group of freedoms.

 

• The Right to Freedom (Articles 19–22) is one of the six Fundamental Rights guaranteed under Part III of the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• “Protection of certain rights regarding freedom of speech, etc.” (Option 1): This is the actual marginal heading of Article 19, a genuine Right to Freedom.

 

• “Protection of life and personal liberty.” (Option 2): This is the marginal heading of Article 21, a genuine Right to Freedom.

 

• “Protection in respect of conviction for offences.” (Option 4): This is the marginal heading of Article 20, a genuine Right to Freedom.

question: International Day for the preservation of the Ozone layer is observed on ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is September 16.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The International Day for the Preservation of the Ozone Layer is observed annually on 16 September, commemorating the signing of the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer in 1987. (ओज़ोन परत के संरक्षण हेतु अंतर्राष्ट्रीय दिवस)

 

• It was designated by the UN General Assembly in 1994 to raise awareness about ozone layer depletion and encourage protective action.

 

• The Montreal Protocol is regarded as one of the most successful international environmental agreements, having phased out nearly 99% of ozone-depleting substances globally.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• World Environment Day is observed on 5 June, and World Earth Day on 22 April — distinct from Ozone Day.

 

• India ratified the Montreal Protocol in 1992.

 

NOTE

 

• September 13 (Option 1): Not a designated UN environmental observance day.

 

• September 10 (Option 2): Not associated with this observance.

 

• September 18 (Option 4): Not the correct date for this observance.

question: The poet - saint Kabir Das was born in ______ sometime in the 15th century.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kashi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kabir Das, the mystic poet-saint, is traditionally believed to have been born in Kashi (Varanasi), sometime in the 15th century. (कबीर दास — काशी)

 

• He was raised by a Muslim weaver couple, Niru and Nima, and later became a disciple of the Bhakti saint Ramananda.

 

• His teachings blended elements of Hinduism, Islam and Sufism, emphasising formless devotion (Nirguna Bhakti) and social equality; his compositions are compiled in the “Bijak.”

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kabir's couplets (dohas) are also included in the Guru Granth Sahib, the holy scripture of Sikhism.

 

• He is considered a key figure of the Bhakti movement and the Nirguna school of Sant poetry.

 

NOTE

 

• Amritsar (Option 2): A city in Punjab, home to the Golden Temple; unrelated to Kabir's birth.

 

• Somnath (Option 3): A town in Gujarat, famous for the Somnath Temple; not linked to Kabir's birth.

 

• Agra (Option 4): A Mughal-era city in Uttar Pradesh, home to the Taj Mahal; not Kabir's birthplace.

question: Which of the following planets is considered as Earth’s twin planet?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Venus.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Venus is called Earth's “twin planet” because of its similar size, mass, density and bulk composition to Earth. (शुक्र ग्रह — पृथ्वी का जुड़वां ग्रह)

 

• Despite these similarities, Venus has a very different atmosphere — a thick, toxic carbon dioxide atmosphere with sulfuric acid clouds, causing an extreme greenhouse effect and surface temperatures around 465°C.

 

• Venus is the second planet from the Sun, the hottest planet in the solar system, and it rotates in a retrograde direction, opposite to most other planets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Venus is the brightest natural object in the night sky after the Moon, often called the “Morning Star” or “Evening Star.”

 

• Its diameter (~12,104 km) is close to Earth's (~12,742 km), reinforcing the “twin” comparison.

 

NOTE

 

• Neptune (Option 1): The eighth and farthest planet from the Sun, an ice giant very different in size and composition from Earth.

 

• Uranus (Option 2): The seventh planet, also an ice giant, much larger and colder than Earth.

 

• Mars (Option 4): Often called the “Red Planet”; smaller than Earth and studied for past habitability, but not considered Earth's “twin” in the way Venus is.

question: On 12 August ______, the Mughal emperor appointed the East India Company as the Diwan of Bengal.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1765.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• On 12 August 1765, the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II granted the Diwani (rights to collect revenue and administer civil justice) of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha to the East India Company through the Treaty of Allahabad. (1765 — दीवानी अधिकार)

 

• This followed the Company's victory at the Battle of Buxar (1764), where Shah Alam II, Mir Qasim (Nawab of Bengal) and Shuja-ud-Daula (Nawab of Awadh) were defeated.

 

• Robert Clive negotiated the treaty on behalf of the East India Company, ushering in the “Dual Government” system in Bengal.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Battle of Plassey (1757) had earlier established British political influence in Bengal.

 

• The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first step by the British Parliament to control Company administration in India.

 

NOTE

 

• 1768 (Option 2): Not linked to any major Diwani-related event.

 

• 1772 (Option 3): The year Warren Hastings became Governor of Bengal and abolished the Dual Government system.

 

• 1760 (Option 4): Not linked to the grant of Diwani; predates the Battle of Buxar.

question: Lovely Choubey is a famous Indian sportswoman associated with ______ sport.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lawn Bowls.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lovely Choubey is an Indian lawn bowls player who was part of the Indian women's fours team that won a historic gold medal at the 2022 Commonwealth Games in Birmingham. (लॉन बाउल्स)

 

• This was India's first-ever medal in lawn bowls at the Commonwealth Games, achieved alongside teammates Pinki, Nayanmoni Saikia and Rupa Rani Tirkey.

 

• She hails from Jharkhand and has represented India in multiple international lawn bowls tournaments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Lawn bowls is a precision sport in which players roll biased balls (“bowls”) to land as close as possible to a smaller target ball (the “jack”).

 

• India's women's fours gold at CWG 2022 was widely celebrated as a breakthrough for a sport that had received little prior attention in the country.

 

NOTE

 

• Table Tennis (Option 1): Notable Indian players include Manika Batra and Sharath Kamal — unrelated to Lovely Choubey.

 

• Cricket (Option 3): India's prominent women cricketers include Mithali Raj and Smriti Mandhana — not Choubey's sport.

 

• Kho-Kho (Option 4): A traditional Indian sport, not associated with Lovely Choubey.

question: Article related to compulsory acquisition of property has been omitted now from the Indian constitution. What is the number of this article?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 31.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 31, which originally guaranteed the Right to Property (including provisions on compulsory acquisition of property), was omitted from Part III (Fundamental Rights) by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978. (अनुच्छेद 31 — संपत्ति का अधिकार)

 

• After its omission, the right to property was retained only as a legal/constitutional right (not a Fundamental Right), under the newly inserted Article 300A.

 

• This change reduced the Fundamental Rights from seven to six, since the Right to Property had earlier been one of them.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 44th Amendment Act, 1978, was enacted under the Janata Party government led by Morarji Desai, largely to reverse some excesses associated with the 42nd Amendment and the Emergency period.

 

• Related provisions such as Articles 31A, 31B and 31C (dealing with land reforms, the Ninth Schedule, and laws implementing Directive Principles) still remain in the Constitution.

 

NOTE

 

• 31D (Option 1): A provision proposed by the 42nd Amendment (relating to anti-national activities) that was itself repealed by the 44th Amendment.

 

• 31B (Option 3): Deals with the validation of Acts and Regulations placed in the Ninth Schedule; still part of the Constitution.

 

• 31A (Option 4): Deals with the saving of laws providing for the acquisition of estates, etc.; still part of the Constitution.

question: Which animal's memorial was inaugurated in September 2022 at Kaziranga National Park in Assam?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rhinoceros.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In September 2022, a Rhino Memorial was inaugurated at Kaziranga National Park, Assam, to honour rhinos that died of natural causes or poaching over the years. (गैंडा स्मारक — काज़ीरंगा राष्ट्रीय उद्यान)

 

• Kaziranga is home to the world's largest population of the Great One-Horned Rhinoceros and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

 

• The memorial was set up as part of ongoing rhino conservation and anti-poaching efforts in the park.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kaziranga National Park, located along the Brahmaputra River in Assam, was declared a National Park in 1974 and a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1985.

 

• India's rhino conservation efforts also include the “Indian Rhino Vision 2020” programme.

 

NOTE

 

• Hippopotamus (Option 2): Not found in the wild in India; unrelated to Kaziranga.

 

• Langur (Option 3): A primate found in India, but not the animal honoured by this memorial.

 

• Gibbon (Option 4): Found in Northeast India (e.g., the Hoolock Gibbon), but not linked to this particular memorial.

question: Which of the following base is found in lime water?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Calcium hydroxide.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lime water is a dilute, aqueous solution of calcium hydroxide, Ca(OH)₂, a mild alkali/base. (चूने का पानी — कैल्शियम हाइड्रॉक्साइड)

 

• It is prepared by dissolving slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) in water and is commonly used to test for the presence of carbon dioxide, which turns lime water milky due to the formation of calcium carbonate.

 

• Lime water has applications in whitewashing, water treatment, and as a mild antacid.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Passing excess CO₂ through lime water eventually clears the milkiness, as soluble calcium bicarbonate is formed.

 

• Quicklime (calcium oxide, CaO) reacts exothermically with water to produce slaked lime (calcium hydroxide).

 

NOTE

 

• Potassium hydroxide (Option 2): A strong base used in soap-making and batteries; not the base in lime water.

 

• Magnesium hydroxide (Option 3): The base found in “milk of magnesia,” used as an antacid; a different compound.

 

• Ammonium hydroxide (Option 4): A weak base formed by dissolving ammonia gas in water; unrelated to lime water.

question: In a drama, Hima spoke “Swaraj is my birth right and I shall have it.”. Which Indian freedom fighter gave this slogan?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bal Gangadhar Tilak.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• “Swaraj is my birthright, and I shall have it” is a famous slogan given by Bal Gangadhar Tilak, a prominent leader of the Indian freedom struggle popularly known as “Lokmanya” (“beloved leader”). (बाल गंगाधर तिलक — स्वराज्य मेरा जन्मसिद्ध अधिकार है)

 

• Tilak first raised this slogan around 1916, during the Home Rule Movement, which he co-founded along with Annie Besant.

 

• He was one of the pioneers of the assertive/“extremist” wing of the Indian National Congress, along with Lal Lajpat Rai and Bipin Chandra Pal (the “Lal-Bal-Pal” trio).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tilak also popularised the public celebration of Ganesh Chaturthi and Shivaji Jayanti as tools for nationalist mobilisation.

 

• He was the editor of the newspapers Kesari (Marathi) and Mahratta (English).

 

NOTE

 

• Bhagat Singh (Option 1): A revolutionary freedom fighter known for actions like the Central Legislative Assembly bombing; not associated with this slogan.

 

• Mahatma Gandhi (Option 3): Known for slogans and movements like “Quit India” and “Do or Die,” but not this particular slogan.

 

• Ambika Charan Majumdar (Option 4): A Congress leader who presided over its 1916 Lucknow session; not associated with coining this slogan.

question: Which of the following shortcut key displays the Editor task pane to check spelling and grammar in the document or the selected text in MS-Word 365?
solution_text:
The correct answer is F7.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In MS-Word 365, pressing F7 opens the Editor task pane, which checks spelling and grammar in the document (or in the selected text). (F7 — वर्तनी और व्याकरण जांच)

 

• The Editor feature in Word 365 replaced the older “Spelling & Grammar” dialog box with a more integrated task-pane experience offering suggestions and style refinements.

 

• F7 has historically been the standard spell-check shortcut across many versions of Microsoft Word.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Shift+F7 opens the Thesaurus for the selected word in MS Word.

 

• F12 opens the “Save As” dialog box in MS Word.

 

NOTE

 

• F1 (Option 2): Opens the Help pane in MS Word.

 

• F10 (Option 3): Activates the Ribbon shortcut keys/key tips display.

 

• F2 (Option 4): Traditionally used (with other keys) to move text or graphics; not the spelling/grammar check shortcut.

question: Who won the Men’s Single title at Wimbledon 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Novak Djokovic.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Novak Djokovic won the Men's Singles title at Wimbledon 2022, defeating Nick Kyrgios in the final. (नोवाक जोकोविच — विंबलडन 2022 विजेता)

 

• This was Djokovic's seventh Wimbledon title and his 21st Grand Slam singles title overall at that point.

 

• The final was played on 10 July 2022 at the All England Club, with Djokovic winning in four sets.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Wimbledon 2022 Women's Singles title was won by Elena Rybakina.

 

• Wimbledon is the oldest Grand Slam tennis tournament, first held in 1877, and the only major still played on grass courts.

 

NOTE

 

• Nick Kyrgios (Option 1): The runner-up at Wimbledon 2022, reaching his first Grand Slam final.

 

• Rafael Nadal (Option 2): Withdrew before the semifinal due to injury in the 2022 edition.

 

• Daniil Medvedev (Option 4): A leading player at the time, but did not play in the 2022 Wimbledon, which barred Russian and Belarusian players following the Russia–Ukraine conflict.

question: Godaan is a novel written by Munshi Premchand, published in the year _______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1936.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Godaan (“The Gift of a Cow”), widely regarded as Munshi Premchand's finest novel, was published in 1936, the same year Premchand passed away. (गोदान — मुंशी प्रेमचंद, 1936)

 

• The novel is considered a landmark of Hindi literature, portraying the struggles of the Indian peasantry through its protagonist, Hori Mahato.

 

• It is regarded as one of the greatest Hindi novels, and has been translated into many languages and adapted for film.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Munshi Premchand (born Dhanpat Rai Srivastava) is regarded as one of the greatest writers of modern Hindi and Urdu literature.

 

• His other notable works include Gaban, Nirmala, Karmabhoomi, and the short story “Kafan.”

 

NOTE

 

• 2006 (Option 1): Far too late; unrelated to Godaan's original publication.

 

• 1976 (Option 3): Incorrect; also long after Premchand's death in 1936.

 

• 1906 (Option 4): Incorrect; predates Premchand's mature literary period and Godaan's actual publication.

question: What is the name of indigenously developed special aviation fuel by the Indian Oil Corporation in September 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is AVGAS 100 LL.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In September 2022, Indian Oil Corporation (IOC) launched AVGAS 100 LL (Aviation Gasoline 100 Low Lead), India's first indigenously developed special aviation fuel for piston-engine aircraft. (एवीएशन गैसोलीन)

 

• It is designed for small piston-engine aircraft and Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs)/drones, unlike ATF (Aviation Turbine Fuel), which powers jet-engine aircraft.

 

• With this launch, IndianOil became the first Indian company to indigenously produce this specialised aviation fuel, reducing dependence on imports.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The launch marked a step toward supporting India's growing general aviation and flying-training sector.

 

• IndianOil already supplies standard ATF (Jet A-1) for commercial jet aircraft across Indian airports.

 

NOTE

 

• LNG 30 (Option 1): Not a real aviation fuel product; LNG (Liquefied Natural Gas) is unrelated to this launch.

 

• CNG 101 (Option 2): CNG (Compressed Natural Gas) is a vehicular fuel, not an aviation fuel product from this launch.

 

• ATF NEW 50 (Option 4): Not an actual product name; standard Aviation Turbine Fuel (ATF) is a separate, pre-existing product used for jet aircraft.
